title: Void Ending in an Opposition to Sun
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The opposition is the hardest figure the Moon can close on: the text grades it as extreme enmity, because the signs it joins stand opposed across all four natural qualities. It shares with the square the warnings that guard every election, and a Moon waning in light and faced by Saturn is the source's own example of a serious misfortune.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with an opposition to Sun, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his light and his generative heat. Picatrix calls the Sun the light of the world and the axis on which the universe turns; generative power flows from him, the heart is his seat in the body, gold is his metal, and the ruby and the jacinth his stones. His benevolence fits great royal achievements and kings. The whole lunar doctrine hangs on him, for in the text's accounting the stars and the Moon together sustain all vegetation and every composite body.
